naics_note: NAICS 2213 (Water/Wastewater Utilities) — task assigns to energy_utilities cell because the canonical f(M) sources are the same family (SAM + EPA + USAspending). Desalination/water-utility-specific corroboration is captured via creative_extensions below.
framework_context: CWCO is a Cayman-incorporated foreign filer (Form 10-K filer) with real operating businesses in Cayman Islands, The Bahamas, BVI and the US. The AIRO-signature hit fires mechanically on 'stock for services' (here = Executive Officer + Director equity-plan grants — legitimate compensation, NOT a fundraising tell) and 'material weakness' (here = ITGC change-management deficiency, remediated Nov 1 2024, no misstatements). The plan tests each claim against the multi-source matrix to verify the framework correctly suppresses the short signal given the operational substance.

claims.claim_text: CWCO and its affiliate operated 10 seawater reverse osmosis desalination plants across Cayman Islands (6, 10.6 MGD), Bahamas (2, 14.8 MGD), and British Virgin Islands (2, 0.8 MGD) — aggregate capacity 26.2 million gallons per day as of December 31, 2024.
claims.source_quote: the number of water production and water treatment plants we and our affiliate operated in each country, and the production capacities of these plants, were as follows: Water Production Plant Location Plants Capacity (1) Cayman Islands 6 10.6 Bahamas 2 14.8 British Virgin Islands 2 0.8 Total 10 26.2 (1) In millions of gallons per day.
claims.subject: Consolidated Water Co. Ltd.

creative_extensions.source_label: Cayman Islands OfReg (Utility Regulation & Competition Office) public licensee register
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.ofreg.ky/ — search registered water utility licensees and concession holders
creative_extensions.rationale: All three Cayman plants (ACWW + West Bay) sit under the 1990 retail license + Feb 18 2025 concession that OfReg administers; absence in OfReg's licensee directory would contradict the exclusive-license claim. Presence is high-confidence corroboration.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: Cayman Water Company Limited registered as licensed water provider for Seven Mile Beach + West Bay service area
creative_extensions.signal_direction: registered_and_active = corroborates; absent = SEVERE contradiction of exclusive-license existence

creative_extensions.source_label: Bahamas Water & Sewerage Corporation (WSC) annual reports / procurement disclosures
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.wsc.com.bs/ — public annual reports identifying contracted bulk-water suppliers and tonnage delivered
creative_extensions.rationale: Windsor (2.8 MGD) and Blue Hills (12.0 MGD) plant deliveries to WSC under minimum-take-or-pay supply agreements should appear in WSC's own bulk-supply disclosures. WSC is the named counterparty for ~25% of CWCO revenue.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: WSC report naming CW-Bahamas / Consolidated Water as bulk supplier with gallons delivered
creative_extensions.signal_direction: named_in_WSC_report = corroborates; absent = MODERATE contradiction (WSC is government agency, disclosure cadence variable)

creative_extensions.source_label: BVI Water and Sewerage Department public bulk-water contract disclosures
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://bvi.gov.vg/ ministry of communications & works publications + BVI Gazette tender awards
creative_extensions.rationale: OC-BVI's 600,000 gpd minimum supply contract with BVI Water & Sewerage (expires March 2031) should appear in BVI government procurement / utility-supply records.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: OC-BVI (Ocean Conversion BVI Ltd) listed as bulk-water supplier to BVIW&S
creative_extensions.signal_direction: present = corroborates; absent = MODERATE (small jurisdiction, sparse disclosure)

claims.extraction_notes: Most CWCO desalination plants are OFFSHORE (Cayman, Bahamas, BVI) so EPA FRS will NOT cover them — absence of those plants in FRS is the expected baseline, NOT a contradiction. Only the US-based PERC/REC/Aerex sites should appear in FRS. This is a Heuristic-1 over-fit risk: the canonical taxonomy primary (EPA) is structurally blind to ~75% of CWCO's plant fleet. The creative extensions (Cayman OfReg, Bahamas WSC, BVI W&S) are the JURISDICTION-CORRECT registries.

claims.claim_text: Kalaeloa Desalco LLC signed a June 2, 2023 definitive agreement with the Honolulu Board of Water Supply to design, build, operate and maintain a 1.7 million gallons-per-day seawater reverse osmosis desalination plant in Oahu, Hawaii; development is currently underway.
claims.source_quote: In September 2021, Kalaeloa Desalco was formed to pursue a project encompassing the design, construction, operations and maintenance of a seawater reverse osmosis desalination plant in Oahu, Hawaii. In June 2023, Kalaeloa Desalco signed a definitive agreement with the Honolulu Board of Water Supply to design, build, operate and maintain a 1.7 million gallons per day seawater reverse osmosis desalination plant in Oahu, Hawaii. Development of this plant is currently underway.
claims.subject: Kalaeloa Desalco LLC
claims.object_value: Honolulu Board of Water Supply / 1.7 MGD plant

creative_extensions.source_label: Honolulu Board of Water Supply procurement records + board meeting minutes
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.boardofwatersupply.com/about-us/board-of-directors/board-meetings — public board minutes & contract awards register
creative_extensions.rationale: BWS is a municipal utility with mandatory public-meeting disclosure of contract awards. A definitive 1.7 MGD desal-plant DBOM contract is a multi-decade procurement that must appear in board minutes and the procurement/contract register.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: BWS board minutes referencing Kalaeloa Desalco award + contract value + milestones
creative_extensions.signal_direction: present = strong corroboration; absent = SEVERE contradiction of a named municipal-utility contract

creative_extensions.source_label: Hawaii Department of Health Safe Drinking Water Branch construction permit register
creative_extensions.rationale: A new 1.7 MGD seawater RO plant requires DOH construction + operating permits. If 'development is currently underway' (2024 filing), DOH should have an open construction permit or pre-construction review record for Kalaeloa Desalco.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: Hawaii DOH permit issued or under review naming Kalaeloa Desalco / BWS Kalaeloa project
creative_extensions.signal_direction: permit_active = corroborates; absent_post_June_2023 = MODERATE (timing may lag; DOH may treat as BWS-owned)

creative_extensions.source_label: USAspending federal-presence check on Kalaeloa Desalco (in case any federal SRF or BIL funding flows through)
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: usaspending.query_federal_presence with name_variants=['Kalaeloa Desalco', 'Consolidated Water', 'Consolidated Water U.S. Holdings', 'PERC Water']
creative_extensions.rationale: Major US desalination projects often receive State Revolving Fund or Bipartisan Infrastructure Law assistance flowed through state agencies that may show in USAspending. Absence is NOT informative (most municipal projects use ratepayer financing), but presence would corroborate scale.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: federal awards / grants associated with Kalaeloa or CW US subsidiaries
creative_extensions.signal_direction: presence = strong corroboration; absence = expected baseline, NOT contradictory

claims.extraction_notes: Honolulu BWS is a municipal-utility customer, not a megacap, so megacap_namecheck would fire false-negative. claim_evolution would be useful for 2024/2025 progress updates but the cleanest direct test is BWS's own public procurement record (creative extension).

claims.claim_text: Aerex Industries owns a 30,000 sq ft manufacturing facility on 6.4 acres in Fort Pierce, Florida, with expansion underway to 47,500 sq ft expected June 2025.
claims.source_quote: Aerex owns a 30,000 square foot manufacturing facility located on 6.4 acres of land in Fort Pierce, Florida and has approximately 6,000 square feet of office space in downtown Fort Pierce under a lease that expires on June 30, 2026. We are in the process of expanding Aerex s manufacturing facility to 47,500 square feet. The anticipated completion date for this expansion is June 2025.
claims.subject: Aerex Industries, Inc.

creative_extensions.source_label: St. Lucie County (FL) Property Appraiser parcel records
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.paslc.gov/ — parcel search by owner 'Aerex Industries' or street address; returns building footprint + permitted SF + use code
creative_extensions.rationale: Direct test of the 30,000 sqft owned-facility claim. County appraiser data shows actual building square footage, parcel size, and recent construction permits — the cleanest possible adjudication of a manufacturing-facility claim.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: parcel owned by Aerex Industries in Fort Pierce with ~6.4 acres + building ~30,000 sqft
creative_extensions.signal_direction: matches = corroborates; missing or much smaller = SEVERE contradiction

creative_extensions.source_label: City of Fort Pierce / St. Lucie County building permit register
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: City of Fort Pierce Community Development permit portal — search recent permits for Aerex Industries expansion
creative_extensions.rationale: A 17,500 sqft manufacturing expansion completing June 2025 requires building permits issued in 2023-2024. Permit history is the operational-capacity test for the claimed expansion timeline.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: active building permit naming Aerex Industries for manufacturing-facility expansion
creative_extensions.signal_direction: permit_issued = corroborates timeline; no_permit_through_2024 = SEVERE contradiction (can't build 17,500sqft in 6 months without permit)

creative_extensions.source_label: OSHA Form 300A establishment search for Aerex Fort Pierce
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: osha_establishments.query_establishments with company_name='Aerex', state='FL', city='Fort Pierce'
creative_extensions.rationale: 30,000 sqft manufacturing plant building reverse-osmosis equipment is plausibly above the 20-employee threshold. OSHA presence would corroborate operational scale; absence is weakly informative for water-equipment OEMs.
creative_extensions.signal_direction: present = corroborates; absent = MODERATE (may be sub-20 emp or industry-exempt)

claims.extraction_notes: This is the SINGLE most testable physical claim in the filing — a US-located, named-address, owned manufacturing facility with a public county-assessor analog. The county-assessor proposal is the canonical operational-capacity test.

claims.claim_text: CW-Bahamas holds long-term bulk-water supply contracts with the Water & Sewerage Corporation of The Bahamas (WSC): Windsor plant (2.8 MGD) expires August 2033 with minimum 16.8 million gallons/week; Blue Hills plant (12.0 MGD) expires March 2032 with minimum 63.0 million gallons/week.
claims.source_quote: Our water supply agreement with the WSC for our Windsor plant, which has a capacity of 2.8 million gallons per day, expires in August 2033 and requires us to deliver and requires the WSC to purchase a minimum of 16.8 million gallons per week. We supply water from the Blue Hills plant, our largest seawater reverse osmosis desalination facility with a capacity of 12.0 million gallons per day, under the terms of a water supply agreement with the WSC that expires in March 2032 that requires us to deliver and requires the WSC to purchase a minimum of 63.0 million gallons of water each week.
claims.subject: CW-Bahamas (Consolidated Water Bahamas Ltd)

creative_extensions.source_label: Water & Sewerage Corporation of The Bahamas annual reports + tariff orders
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.wsc.com.bs/ — WSC annual report and operations review identifying bulk-water suppliers and minimum-take volumes
creative_extensions.rationale: WSC is the named counterparty. Its own operating reports should disclose suppliers, including the take-or-pay minimum volumes. A government water utility purchasing ~80 million gallons per week from one supplier WILL appear in its own audited reports.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: WSC annual report listing CW-Bahamas / Consolidated Water as supplier of Windsor + Blue Hills with gallons purchased
creative_extensions.signal_direction: present = strong corroboration; absent = SEVERE contradiction of named-counterparty + dollar-magnitude claim

creative_extensions.source_label: Central Bank of The Bahamas exchange-control approvals registry
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.centralbankbahamas.com/ — exchange control statistics on USD remittances to non-resident parents
creative_extensions.rationale: Filing says transfers from Bahamian bank accounts need Central Bank approval. CW-Bahamas remitting upstream to parent would create a documented exchange-control trail proxying the real cash flow scale.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: approved upstream USD remittances from CW-Bahamas
creative_extensions.signal_direction: consistent_magnitude = corroborates real cash conversion; absent = MODERATE (private central-bank data, not all approvals public)

creative_extensions.source_label: Bahamas International Securities Exchange (BISX) — Bahamian Depository Receipts on Consolidated Water
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.bisxbahamas.com/ — BDR trading data and listing disclosures (2,023,850 BDRs representing 404,770 common shares)
creative_extensions.rationale: BISX listing creates a second-jurisdiction disclosure obligation. The Bahamian listing authority would have audited financial filings that triangulate CW-Bahamas's reported revenue from WSC.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: BISX-filed financial statements consistent with US 10-K segment disclosures for Bahamas
creative_extensions.signal_direction: consistent = corroborates; divergent_segment_revenue = SEVERE financial-statement integrity contradiction

claims.extraction_notes: WSC is a sovereign water authority, not a US megacap. Heuristic-7 (counterparty 10-K disclosure) is structurally inapplicable. claim_evolution is the framework-internal default; the creative extension to WSC's own reports is the JURISDICTION-CORRECT test.

claims.claim_text: Cayman Water received a new concession from the Cayman Islands government on February 18, 2025 that authorizes and maintains the terms of the 1990 retail license until a new license is negotiated with OfReg.
claims.source_quote: On February 18, 2025, Cayman Water received a new concession from the government that authorizes and maintains the terms of the 1990 license until a new license from OfReg is negotiated and enacted.
claims.subject: Cayman Water Company Limited

proposed_connector.description: Cayman Islands Utility Regulation & Competition Office (OfReg) public licensee + concession register

proposed_connector.completeness: all Cayman utility licensees (water, electricity, ICT) within OfReg's mandate

creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://www.gov.ky/ — Cayman Gazette publishes statutory instruments including utility concessions

creative_extensions.expected_observable: Gazette notice dated Feb 18 2025 granting concession to Cayman Water Company Limited

claims.claim_text: REC (Ramey Environmental Compliance) performed operations, maintenance, and monitoring services for 64 wastewater and water treatment plants located in the Rocky Mountain and Eastern Plains Regions of Colorado as of December 31, 2024 (down from 72 in 2023).
claims.source_quote: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, REC performed operations, maintenance, and monitoring services for 64 and 72, respectively, wastewater and water treatment plants located in the Rocky Mountain and Eastern Plains Regions of Colorado.
claims.subject: Ramey Environmental Compliance, Inc.

creative_extensions.source_label: Colorado Department of Public Health & Environment (CDPHE) Water Quality Control Division — certified operator registry
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://cdphe.colorado.gov/wqcd-operator-certification — registry of certified water/wastewater operators and the systems they operate
creative_extensions.rationale: Every Colorado wastewater/water plant requires a CDPHE-certified operator. REC's named-operator coverage of 64 plants creates a direct registry footprint. The 72->64 decline is testable as a real contract-attrition signal vs an inflated claim.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: REC / Ramey Environmental named as operator-of-record on ~64 Colorado plants
creative_extensions.signal_direction: matches_count = strong corroboration; many fewer = SEVERE production_volume contradiction; many more = expected (operators may be on contracts not yet disclosed)

creative_extensions.source_label: EPA Safe Drinking Water Information System (SDWIS) public water system registry
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: https://enviro.epa.gov/envirofacts/sdwis — public water system records filtered to Colorado
creative_extensions.rationale: Every public water system files with SDWIS. Cross-checking against CDPHE adds federal corroboration of operator-of-record assignments.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: PWSs in CO Rocky Mountain / Eastern Plains regions with REC contractor flag
creative_extensions.signal_direction: present = corroborates plant-count footprint; absent = MODERATE (contractor identity not always in SDWIS)

claims.extraction_notes: EPA emissions/FRS is the canonical primary but is structurally noisy for small-municipal-water O&M (operators don't always appear as 'facilities' in FRS). The state-level CDPHE registry is the operational-correct registry. The 72->64 YoY decline is itself a soft self-disclosed honesty signal — companies inflating customer counts don't typically disclose contract attrition.

claims.claim_text: A material weakness in internal control over financial reporting was identified as of December 31, 2024, related to insufficient information technology general controls over change management to two accounting-system databases during January 1 - October 31, 2024; remediation was completed effective November 1, 2024 with no identified misstatements.
claims.source_quote: A material weakness was identified in our internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2024. The material weakness related to insufficient information technology general controls designed to monitor direct changes to databases within two accounting systems during the period January 1, 2024 through October 31, 2024. ... Effective November 1, 2024, the deficiency was remediated. ... The referenced deficiency did not result in any identified misstatements to the consolidated financial statements, and there were no changes to previously released financial results.
claims.subject: Consolidated Water Co. Ltd.
claims.object_value: ITGC change-management; remediated Nov 1 2024; no misstatements

creative_extensions.source_label: SEC EDGAR — focal company filing-cadence check for Item 4.02 (Non-Reliance) or NT-10 filings
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: sec_filings.list_filings_by_form with cik=0000928340, forms=['NT 10-K','NT 10-Q','8-K'] looking for Item 4.02 across 2018-2025
creative_extensions.rationale: True distress-clustering would show LATE filings (NT 10-K, NT 10-Q) and/or Item 4.02 non-reliance 8-Ks alongside the material-weakness disclosure. The filing was on time (March 17, 2025), with no Item 4.02, suggesting an isolated ITGC issue rather than a distress cluster. Heuristic-10 calibration test.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: any NT filings or Item 4.02 8-Ks in 2024-2025
creative_extensions.signal_direction: none_found = corroborates isolated technical deficiency (NOT distress); multiple_NT_or_4.02 = elevates to genuine distress cluster

creative_extensions.source_label: Going-concern paragraph + auditor changes + reverse-split + ATM offerings cross-check
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: edgar_fts.query_fulltext with search_term='going concern' cik=0000928340; sec_filings.list_filings_by_form for S-3/424B prospectus supplements; 10-K Item 9 changes-in-accountants
creative_extensions.rationale: Heuristic-10 explicitly requires >=2 clustered distress markers within ~6 months for the material-weakness flag to fire. CWCO has paid dividends continuously since 1985 (now $0.41/yr) and the 10-K explicitly says NO misstatements — a single ITGC weakness with prompt remediation does NOT cluster with going-concern / reverse-split / ATM markers.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: no going-concern paragraph; no reverse split; no ATM in 2024; same auditor
creative_extensions.signal_direction: all_absent = correctly suppresses single-marker false positive; if_clustered = real distress signal

claims.extraction_notes: CRITICAL Heuristic-10 calibration test. The 'material weakness' phrase is the mechanical trigger of the AIRO-signature screen, but the substance is a remediated ITGC change-management issue with NO misstatements. Combined with continuous dividends since 1985, this should NOT cluster as financial_distress. The framework's job is to verify the absence of corroborating distress markers.

claims.claim_text: Equity-based compensation: 24,875 shares issued January 2, 2025 to Executive Officers under the 2008 Equity Incentive Plan, plus 11,448 shares to Directors on December 17, 2024 under the Non-Executive Directors Share Plan; total issuance ~92,457 shares to officers in 2024-2025 plus director grants.
claims.source_quote: On January 2, 2024, March 27, 2024 and January 2, 2025, we issued a total of 29,392 shares, 26,742 shares and 24,875 shares of our common stock, respectively, to Executive Officers under our 2008 Equity Incentive Plan. On December 17, 2024, we issued a total of 11,448 shares of our common stock to our Directors under our Non-Executive Directors Share Plan in consideration for their service on our Board of Directors and the committees thereof.
claims.subject: Consolidated Water Co. Ltd.
claims.object_value: ~92,457 shares to officers + 11,448 to directors under registered equity plans

creative_extensions.source_label: SEC Form 4 / Form 5 insider transaction filings
creative_extensions.endpoint_or_method: sec_filings.list_filings_by_form with cik=0000928340, forms=['4','5'] to verify each named officer/director Form 4 against the 10-K disclosure
creative_extensions.rationale: Section 16 insiders must file Form 4 within 2 business days of each grant. The 24,875+11,448-share grants should match individual Form 4 filings on January 2 2025 / December 17 2024. Mismatch would suggest fabricated or unauthorized issuance.
creative_extensions.expected_observable: Form 4 filings on the named dates summing to the disclosed share counts
creative_extensions.signal_direction: matches = corroborates legitimate equity comp; missing_Form_4 = SEVERE contradiction (Section 16 violation)

claims.extraction_notes: CRITICAL AIRO-signature calibration. The 'stock for services' phrase is the mechanical trigger, but the SUBSTANCE here is routine 2008 Equity Incentive Plan officer grants + Non-Executive Directors Share Plan grants — i.e., legitimate compensation under SEC-registered plans, NOT fundraising-via-services-for-shares. The total ~104k shares represents an immaterial fraction of float (CWCO has 695 holders of record and ~16M shares outstanding ~ 0.65% dilution). Status=NONE because there's no external registry that adjudicates 'is this an inflation tell vs legitimate comp'; the discriminator is the SUBSTANCE of the equity-plan disclosure (registered S-8 plan, named insiders, Form-4-filed) which IS in EDGAR. Creative extension proposes the Form 4 cross-check.
